_comment: Reference example — copy values into loop.config.json and edit. Every field is documented inline below. Optional fields may be null; the loop degrades gracefully (e.g. no headroom signal => the loop keeps ticking and notes the gauge is stale; no validator => the reconcile step is a no-op).
_ship_root: Absolute path to your ship directory (where queue.md, captain.md, projects/, logs/, state/ live). The skills resolve all ship paths from here. '.' means the current working directory.
_repos: The repos crew work in. Used for the preflight git-status sweep (catch uncommitted work) and for orienting dispatch. Empty list is valid — the git sweep just skips.
_max_concurrent_crew: Cap on simultaneously-dispatched crew. A flat default. Rate/cost-aware dispatch bands (varying the cap by available headroom) are a module on top, not core.
_chat_surface: Where directives arrive that should WAKE the loop (vs. just batch). 'kind' is informational: 'file' (watch a file/dir), 'http' (poll/subscribe an endpoint), or null (inbox edits + crew completions are the only wake sources). classify_input.py decides wake-vs-batch; this points the wake-monitor at the surface. A status-surface UI module typically provides an http thread endpoint here.
_headroom_signal_path: Optional path to a JSON file carrying a context-headroom reading (e.g. {"pct_used": 0.42, "ts": "<ISO>"}) written by a statusline hook. The wind-down rule reads this as signal (a). Absent => the loop cannot use signal (a); it keeps ticking and notes gauge=stale, winding down only on a compaction warning or Captain order.
_validator_cmd: Optional command run at the reconcile step. Should exit 0 / print a parseable RESULT line for CLEAN, non-zero / MISMATCH otherwise. Absent => reconcile is a no-op and validator is reported as 'NONE'. Frontmatter/view validators are a module; the reconcile STEP is core, the validator itself is an add-on.
_hosts_ports: Optional. Only used by UI/status-surface modules (the headless loop needs none of this). Lists the local hosts/ports a module serves on, so the preflight can check 'is the surface up?'. Leave null for a headless loop.
